headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage: Airbyte’s broad egress can move business data while Whisper has no network or filesystem defenses, but prompt injection and capability conflict are largely blocked by the profiles.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible default injection bridge is documented. Airbyte has broad network egress, but Whisper has no clipboard, MCP, filesystem read/write, or stdin/stdout surface, so there is no clear channel for Airbyte output to be parsed as instructions by Whisper. Uncertainty is low because both profiles explicitly lack shared channels.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or message queue is added between the agents, injection risk becomes plausible.
IF Whisper is wrapped in a parser that treats Airbyte output as instructions, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate runtimes with no shared clipboard or queue.
Do not pipe Airbyte output directly into any instruction-following prompt.
Add a manual review step before any downstream action.
requires-engineering: enforce provenance tags on all inter-agent messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress, so it can move sensitive content off-host by default. Whisper touches audio/speech and has no network egress, but the pair still creates a leakage path if business data is routed into Airbyte and then forwarded externally. The interaction is inferred from profiles, so uncertainty remains.
conditions: IF business data is ingested into Airbyte and sent to an external destination, leakage occurs.
IF audio files contain business data and are transcribed into Airbyte-managed pipelines, the same risk applies.
mitigations: Restrict Airbyte destinations to approved internal endpoints.
Separate business-data pipelines from any audio transcription workflow.
Review connector configs for outbound transfers before enabling them.
Mask or redact sensitive fields before ingestion.
requires-engineering: add DLP controls on Airbyte egress.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No write-write conflict is evident. Airbyte exposes only an API and broad network egress; Whisper has no filesystem write, git, subprocess, or network capabilities. Without overlapping mutable surfaces, the pair cannot contend over shared state in the documented profiles.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or git repo, reassess conflict risk.
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable OAuth scopes, conflict risk may emerge.
mitigations: Keep Whisper read-only and offline.
Avoid mounting a shared writable workspace.
Do not grant Airbyte and Whisper overlapping credentials.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared state is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: There is no documented default pipeline where Whisper’s output is automatically treated as authoritative by Airbyte. Airbyte is a data-integration system, while Whisper is a speech model with no action-taking authority. Any cascade would require an external orchestrator to chain them, so the pathway is possible but not default.
conditions: IF an orchestrator feeds Whisper transcripts directly into Airbyte jobs without validation, cascading errors become plausible.
IF Airbyte is configured to act on Whisper-generated labels or commands, downstream mistakes can propagate.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before Airbyte ingestion.
Validate Whisper transcripts against expected schemas.
Use confidence thresholds before acting on transcriptions.
Log and diff transformed records before sync.
requires-engineering: add automated verification between transcription and ETL.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and only document business data versus audio/speech, with no residency, certification, or retention mismatch stated. Because no compliance gap is documented, the risk is limited to potential policy mismatch if the operator routes regulated data through Airbyte or Whisper. The other agent is not cited beyond its data class because no specific compliance claim exists.
conditions: IF regulated audio or business data is routed through a policy-restricted environment, compliance review is required.
IF retention or residency requirements differ between the two pipelines, reassess upward.
mitigations: Confirm data classification before processing.
Keep regulated data out of both tools unless approved.
Document retention settings for each pipeline.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention enforcement.
